channel.title: Wander Notes
channel.description: Travel stories, itineraries and practical tips from the road by Adarsh Nair: where to go, how to get around and what it really costs.

item.title: As large as Rome: the rise and fall of Vijayanagara at Hampi
item.description: Five hundred years ago, among the giant boulders of Hampi, stood one of the richest cities on Earth, where diamonds were sold in the open street. Then, in a single afternoon in 1565, it lost everything. Here's the story of Vijayanagara: the brothers who founded it, the poet-king who made it shine, the battle that ended it and the ruins that remain.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: How I got my full ₹15,000 back after SpiceJet cancelled my flight (and Goibibo refunded ₹2,526)
item.description: SpiceJet cancelled our Delhi–Bengaluru flight and Goibibo offered back ₹2,526 of the ₹15,000 we paid. Here's exactly how I escalated it, what finally worked, the passenger rules that apply, and templates you can copy for your own SpiceJet refund complaint.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: South Korea in eight days from Bengaluru: Seoul, Gyeongju and Busan
item.description: Eight days in South Korea from Bengaluru: Seoul's palaces, hanok lanes and a DMZ day trip, Gyeongju's thousand-year-old Silla capital, and Busan's temples, beaches and fish market, with the visa for Indians, flights, KTX trains, vegetarian tips, checked hotels and costs in rupees.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Kerala's coast in five days from Bengaluru: Kochi, Alleppey, Varkala and Thiruvananthapuram
item.description: A five-day road trip down Kerala's coast from Bengaluru: Fort Kochi's fishing nets, a houseboat on the Alleppey backwaters, palpayasam at Ambalappuzha, the cliffs of Varkala, the giant Jatayu sculpture and the Padmanabhaswamy temple, with trains, drive times, checked hotels and costs in rupees.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Dubai in five days from India: towers, souks, dunes and the Creek
item.description: Five days in Dubai from India: the Burj Khalifa, the old Creek and souks, a desert evening and Global Village, with visa rules, metro fares, checked hotels and costs in rupees for winter 2026.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The village without doors: the story of Shani Shingnapur
item.description: In a farming village in Maharashtra, a black stone stands under the open sky, and for generations the houses around it had no front doors. The villagers said the god in the stone would punish any thief. Here's the legend, what happened when the locks crept back, and the fight over who may touch the stone.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The lake of bones: the mystery of Roopkund in the Himalayas
item.description: High in the Himalayas, a small glacial lake gives up hundreds of human skeletons every summer. For decades people blamed a royal pilgrimage, a hailstorm or a lost army. Then DNA showed the dead came from different centuries, and some from the far side of the Mediterranean.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Morocco for the 2027 Eclipse: The Budget Alternative to Spain
item.description: On 2 August 2027 the Moon's shadow crosses the Strait of Gibraltar. Southern Spain's eclipse hotels already cost thousands, but across the water in northern Morocco totality lasts longer and rooms still cost under $150. Here's a seven-day plan through Tangier and Chefchaouen, with timings, weather odds and checked hotels.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The temple carved from the top down: the story of Kailasa at Ellora
item.description: Twelve hundred years ago, sculptors in western India climbed onto a hill of solid rock and began cutting downwards. When they stopped, they had carved a complete, multi-story temple out of a single stone. This is the story of Kailasa, its legends, and how they really did it.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Seychelles in ten days: Mahé, Praslin and La Digue by ferry and bike
item.description: Ten days in the Seychelles from the US: Mahé's mountains and reefs, Praslin's coco de mer forest, and La Digue by bike, with ferry fares, real prices in dollars, checked hotels and the boat trips worth booking.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Kerala in fifteen days over Christmas: Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and the backwaters
item.description: Fifteen days in Kerala over Christmas and New Year from the US: Fort Kochi's churches and star lanterns, Christmas Eve in the tea hills of Munnar, Periyar's forest, a night on a backwater houseboat and quiet days on Marari beach, with flights, the e-Visa, prices in dollars and checked stays.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Thailand in ten days over Christmas: Chiang Mai, Bangkok and Krabi
item.description: Ten days in Thailand over Christmas week from the US: cool mornings and night markets in Chiang Mai, the Grand Palace and Chinatown in Bangkok, and Christmas Day on Railay's beaches in Krabi, with flights, the new 30-day entry rule, prices in dollars, checked hotels and what sells out first.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Bali in twelve days: Ubud, Sidemen, Nusa Lembongan and Uluwatu
item.description: Twelve days in Bali from the US, beyond the party strip: rice terraces and a sunrise volcano hike from Ubud, a quiet valley under Mount Agung in Sidemen, the cliffs of Nusa Penida from Lembongan, and Uluwatu's surf beaches and fire dance, with flights, visa rules, prices in dollars and checked stays.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Kashmir in five nights from Delhi: Srinagar, Gulmarg and Pahalgam
item.description: Five nights in Kashmir from Delhi: a houseboat and shikara mornings on Dal Lake, Srinagar's Mughal gardens and old city, the Gulmarg gondola, and Pahalgam's Betaab and Aru valleys, with flight and train options, real costs, checked stays and what's open right now.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The lost gospel of Hemis: a monastery in Ladakh and the story of Jesus in India
item.description: In 1894, a Russian traveler published a sensational book claiming he had seen, in a monastery high in Ladakh, ancient scrolls describing Jesus's lost years in India. The world was gripped. Then a professor went to the monastery and asked. Here is the story of Hemis, its masked dances and its giant painting, and the manuscript nobody else ever saw.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Finnish Lapland in ten days: Helsinki, Rovaniemi and Saariselkä in January
item.description: Ten winter days in Finland from the US: a night in Helsinki, the Santa Claus Express to Rovaniemi, then north to Saariselkä and Inari for huskies, reindeer, snowshoes and the northern lights, with real prices in dollars, checked hotels and the tours worth booking.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Japan in twelve days: Tokyo, Hakone, Kyoto, Hiroshima and Osaka
item.description: A twelve-day first trip to Japan by bullet train: four nights in Tokyo, an onsen night in Hakone, three in Kyoto, one in Hiroshima and two in Osaka, with real fares, checked hotels, the Klook tickets and codes worth using, and why you can skip the JR Pass.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Bridges that grow: the living root bridges of Meghalaya
item.description: In one of the wettest places on Earth, the Khasi people don't build bridges. They grow them, training the roots of fig trees across rivers over decades until they can carry dozens of people. Some are well over a century old and still getting stronger. Here is how they're made, who made them, and the stories around them.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The temple named after its sculptor: Ramappa and the bricks that float
item.description: In 1213, a general of the Kakatiya kings built a temple to Shiva beside a lake in Telangana, with a tower of bricks so light they float, foundations of sand, and black stone dancers polished like mirrors. Eight hundred years later it became India's 39th World Heritage Site. Here is its story.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Taipei, Taitung and Kaohsiung: five days down Taiwan's east coast
item.description: Five days and four nights in Taiwan: two nights in Taipei, the train down the east coast to Taitung, then the South-Link line to Kaohsiung, with real fares, checked hotels, Klook tickets worth booking and the closures to plan around.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Found by a tiger hunter: the painted caves of Ajanta
item.description: In April 1819, a British cavalry officer chasing a tiger looked across a ravine in Maharashtra and saw a row of carved doorways in the cliff. Behind them, in the dark, were Buddhist paintings fifteen hundred years old. Here is how monks and an emperor's ministers made Ajanta, why it was abandoned, and how it was nearly lost again.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The king's great temple: a thousand years of Brihadeeswarar at Thanjavur
item.description: In the year 1010, a Chola king finished a granite tower more than 200 feet tall, crowned with a stone said to weigh 80 tons, and wrote down every gift, every dancer and every lamp on its walls. A thousand years later, worship still goes on inside. Here is how Rajaraja built the Big Temple, and the myths that grew around it.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Bengaluru to Wayanad: four days of forests, caves and coffee
item.description: A four-day road trip from Bengaluru through Bandipur to Wayanad: Edakkal's carved cave, a jeep safari in Muthanga, Banasura's reservoir, Thirunelli and Kuruva, with real bus fares, safari timings and the night-ban rules you need to plan around.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The great university of Nalanda, and the fire that may not have happened
item.description: For seven hundred years, monks and scholars from across Asia walked to a brick university in Bihar to study philosophy, logic and medicine. Then it vanished. The famous story says a raider burned its library for months. The record is more complicated, and more interesting.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The pillar that doesn't touch the ground: the legends of Lepakshi
item.description: Two hours from Bengaluru, a 16th-century temple has a pillar you can slide a cloth under, a giant stone bull, painted ceilings, a seven-headed serpent carved before lunch, and two red stains said to be a governor's blinded eyes. Here is the story of Lepakshi, from the wounded bird of the Ramayana to the brothers who built it.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Bengaluru to the sea: six days down the Karnataka coast
item.description: A six-day route from Bengaluru through the Western Ghats to Mangaluru, Udupi, Murudeshwar and Gokarna, with real fares, ferry timings and what to eat at every stop.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Hampi: Three Days Among Ancient Ruins and Boulders
item.description: Explore Hampi, the ancient Vijayanagara capital, with our 3-day guide. From scooter rides across the river to iconic sunsets and coracle adventures.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: Gone by sunset: the true story behind Bhangarh, India's 'most haunted' fort
item.description: In the hills of Rajasthan stands a 400-year-old town of roofless houses, empty temples and a ruined palace, with a government sign telling visitors to leave before dark. The legends blame a sorcerer and a holy man's curse. The history is quieter, and in some ways sadder.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: The queen's stepwell: how Rani ki Vav vanished under the mud and came back
item.description: In 11th-century Gujarat, a widowed queen built a temple upside down: seven stories of carved stone stepping down to water. Then the river flooded, the well filled with silt, and for 700 years almost nobody knew what lay beneath the fields of Patan.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)

item.title: A chariot for the sun: the story of the Konark Sun Temple
item.description: On the coast of Odisha, a 13th-century king built the sun god a stone chariot with twenty-four wheels and seven horses. Its great tower fell centuries ago, sailors called what was left the Black Pagoda, and the British filled the rest with sand. Here is how it was built, why it fell, and the legends that grew in the ruins.
item.author: adarshnair01@gmail.com (Adarsh Nair)
